metadata.title: Kent LGBTQ+ Homelessness Resource Database
metadata.note: Resolve DATA-001 and update Samaritans 2026 contact transition. Parent version: v1. Re-check provider routes before production release.

services.name: Emergency services
services.referral: Call; if unable to speak on a mobile, press 55 when prompted.
services.notes: Use where life, safety or serious crime is at immediate risk.

services.name: NHS 111
services.type: Urgent health and mental health triage
services.referral: Call 111 and select the mental-health option when offered.
services.notes: Not a substitute for 999 where there is immediate danger.

services.name: StreetLink
services.tags: rough sleeping|street outreach|concern for another person
services.referral: Self-report or report someone; give a precise location and appearance only with consent where possible.
services.notes: An alert is not a guaranteed bed; also contact the local council where there is immediate need.

services.name: Porchlight rough sleeper service
services.referral: Self-referral by phone; ask about local outreach, housing support and safe contact arrangements.
services.notes: Kent-wide homelessness charity; confirm availability for the person’s district.

services.name: Catching Lives
services.type: Day centre, survival support and advocacy
services.referral: Attend or contact the charity; app should show current opening hours before directing travel.
services.notes: Supports people who are homeless or insecurely housed in Canterbury and East Kent.

services.name: RISE rough sleeping partnership
services.referral: Complete a Homeless Approach with Housing Options; if not offered priority housing, ask about RISE referral.
services.notes: A navigator may support appointments, affordability and tenancy move-in.

services.name: Salvation Army Tunbridge Wells Corps
services.hours: Wed-Thu before midday; confirm before travel
services.referral: Drop in; app must display the council page and a verify-time warning.
services.notes: Listed by Tunbridge Wells Borough Council; not accommodation.

services.name: Kent Homechoice
services.referral: Create an account; complete pre-assessment and upload evidence. Do not treat as an emergency accommodation route.
services.notes: District eligibility and allocation rules differ; housing register is not a same-night solution.

services.name: Shelter emergency helpline
services.type: Housing rights, homelessness and abuse-at-home advice
services.referral: Call, use webchat or self-help. Keep calling if lines are busy.
services.notes: Shelter advises but does not provide accommodation directly.

services.name: Citizens Advice housing and homelessness advice
services.type: Housing, welfare, debt and legal-information advice
services.referral: Use national advice and route to the relevant local Citizens Advice office; ask for an accessibility adjustment if needed.
services.notes: The app should use a local-office lookup for appointment availability.

services.name: Citizens Advice in North & West Kent
services.coverage: Dartford, Gravesham, Sevenoaks, Tonbridge and Malling, Tunbridge Wells
services.referral: Call the Adviceline or use the local office / Kent Advice Hub route.
services.notes: Phone number and route verified through Tunbridge Wells Council.

services.name: Civil Legal Advice
services.referral: Check eligibility online or call. Relay UK: 18001 then 0345 345 4345.
services.notes: Legal aid can cover homelessness, eviction, loss of home and serious disrepair where eligibility is met.

services.name: Housing Loss Prevention Advice Service
services.referral: Use if a written possession claim / hearing exists; no means test for the court-duty service.
services.notes: Link to the government directory in the app rather than listing time-sensitive provider details.

services.name: Homeless England service directory
services.type: Searchable accommodation and homelessness services directory
services.referral: Search by postcode and service type; validate availability directly with providers.
services.notes: Directory record is not evidence of a vacancy or immediate eligibility.

services.name: akt
services.type: LGBTQ+ youth homelessness and hostile-home support
services.referral: Self-refer; explain immediate safety, age, location, family rejection and housing situation.
services.notes: For LGBTQ+ people aged 16-25 who are homeless or facing a hostile living environment.

services.name: Stonewall Housing advice line
services.type: Specialist LGBTQ+ housing advice and advocacy
services.referral: Call, use live chat or submit referral. Ask for advocacy where a council or landlord is not engaging.
services.notes: Nationwide free specialist housing advice for LGBTQ+ people of every age.

services.name: Galop LGBT+ Abuse and Violence Helpline
services.type: LGBT+ domestic abuse, hate crime and sexual-violence support
services.referral: Call or email; explain if the unsafe person can monitor devices and request safe-contact planning.
services.notes: For LGBT+ people, supporters and professionals. App should show a quick-exit button and privacy warning.

services.name: LGBT Foundation Helpline
services.referral: Call or email for direct support and signposting.
services.notes: Useful parallel support while housing action is underway.

services.name: MGSD Centre
services.type: LGBTQI+ counselling, peer support and safe spaces
services.referral: Use Kent Connect to Support listing and contact the Centre.
services.notes: A Kent-specific LGBTQI+ organisation; keep contact fields refreshed through the provider.

services.name: BeYou Project
services.referral: Use the NHS Kent Community Health page to find the current project contact / sessions.
services.notes: Not a housing service; add alongside statutory youth-homelessness action.

services.name: Release the Pressure
services.provider: Rethink Mental Illness / Kent County Council
services.referral: Call; text KENT or MEDWAY to 85258; app should ask about immediate safety first.
services.notes: Free and confidential. Call 999 if life is at immediate risk.

services.name: Shout
services.referral: Text SHOUT to 85258; Kent users can also text KENT or MEDWAY as directed locally.
services.notes: Useful when speaking aloud is unsafe or inaccessible.

services.name: Samaritans
services.referral: Call free on 116 123 at any time. If there is an immediate threat to life or a serious medical emergency, call 999.
services.notes: No requirement to be suicidal to call. Samaritans is an emotional-support service and does not provide accommodation, housing advice or emergency medical treatment. The UK email service is closing during 2026 and must not be displayed as a standard route for new users.

services.name: GP registration without fixed address
services.referral: Tell the surgery you are of no fixed abode / temporarily local. A GP can register you without proof of address or ID.
services.notes: Ask for a clinician letter if health or disability affects housing; do not delay urgent treatment for registration.

services.name: Kent sexual health service
services.provider: Kent Community Health NHS Foundation Trust
services.type: Free confidential sexual health advice and clinics
services.referral: Call or use the service site to find the appropriate clinic; privacy and safety needs can be discussed.
services.notes: Use alongside GP or NHS 111 for urgent symptoms.

services.name: Kent and Medway Domestic Abuse Partnership
services.type: Domestic abuse safety planning and local specialist routes
services.referral: Use the local support finder and safety-planning guidance. Call 999 if in immediate danger.
services.notes: Support is free and confidential; device-safety guidance is essential.

services.name: Medway Domestic Abuse Service
services.referral: Self-refer by phone/email; state any immediate housing need and safe contact method.
services.notes: For Medway residents or people seeking help in Medway.

services.name: Men's Advice Line
services.referral: Call, email or webchat; can support men and people supporting them.
services.notes: Gender identity and sexual orientation must never be assumed; offer Galop too where relevant.

services.name: Victim Support Kent and Medway
services.referral: Self-refer or contact after reporting; support is available whether or not police are involved.
services.notes: KMDAP routes often direct to Victim Support for specialist domestic-abuse support.

services.name: Kent Support and Assistance Service
services.referral: Apply after checking other support options; support is essential items, not cash.
services.notes: The Household Support Fund ended; the Crisis and Resilience Fund succeeded it. Keep funding status live.

services.name: Kent Crisis and Resilience Fund
services.referral: Check current application routes through KCC / district council and record outcome.
services.notes: Scheme and local delivery routes are time-sensitive; needs frequent verification.

services.name: Kent food-bank finder
services.referral: Search local food support and ask whether a referral voucher is needed.
services.notes: The app should display travel distance, eligibility and referral requirements from verified provider records.

services.name: Live Well Kent & Medway
services.type: Wellbeing navigation, housing, debt and employment support
services.referral: Call for a navigator; state housing risk and any mental-health / accessibility needs.
services.notes: Useful for tenancy sustainment and connected needs; it may require an existing tenancy for some local housing support.

services.name: StepChange debt advice
services.referral: Use online debt advice or call; tell them rent, council tax and energy arrears are priority debts.
services.notes: Not a housing provider; pair with council housing options.

services.name: National Debtline
services.referral: Call or use webchat; prepare income, debts and any eviction paperwork.
services.notes: Support is confidential and free.

services.name: Turn2us grants and benefits checker
services.referral: Use benefits calculator and grants search; app should not promise eligibility.
services.notes: Useful for small stabilising grants, but never delay statutory homelessness presentation.

services.name: Jobcentre Plus / Universal Credit
services.type: Income, advance payment and work support
services.referral: Use an existing UC journal if possible; request an advance only after understanding repayment impact.
services.notes: A public authority may have a Duty to Refer role with consent when homelessness risk is identified.

services.name: West Kent Drug and Alcohol Wellbeing Service
services.coverage: Dartford, Gravesham, Maidstone, Sevenoaks, Tonbridge and Malling, Tunbridge Wells
services.referral: Self-refer; state housing risk, medication / prescribing needs and safe contact preferences.
services.notes: Free and confidential. Do not make abstinence a condition for showing housing options.

services.name: WithYou Kent drug and alcohol support for under-25s
services.type: Young people's drug and alcohol support
services.referral: Self / professional referral through the Kent hub; use alongside youth-homelessness route.
services.notes: For young people and families; confirm current geographic and age eligibility.

services.name: FRANK
services.referral: Use for information and immediate signposting; in overdose or emergency call 999.
services.notes: Not a substitute for local treatment or emergency services.

services.name: Centrepoint Helpline
services.referral: Call for advice and connection; local council remains the first statutory route within 56 days or when homeless.
services.notes: Adults supporting a person under 25 can also call.

services.name: Kent Children's Social Care
services.type: Safeguarding and accommodation duty for children
services.hours: Out-of-hours number; normal-hours route on page
services.referral: If under 18 has nowhere safe to stay, contact Children's Social Care immediately; call 999 for immediate danger.
services.notes: Do not route an under-18 person solely to adult homelessness services.

services.name: Medway youth homelessness support
services.type: Youth homelessness and Children's Services route
services.referral: Use the council youth-homelessness route and ask Children's Services for a safe-accommodation assessment.
services.notes: Keep this separate from the adult Medway homelessness route.

services.name: Nacro criminal record and resettlement support
services.referral: Call before release where possible; ask prison / probation to make a Duty to Refer with consent.
services.notes: Availability of direct accommodation varies by area; app must distinguish information from local placements.

services.name: Probation / prison Duty to Refer
services.provider: HM Prison and Probation Service / local council
services.tags: prison leaver|probation|duty to refer|homelessness within 56 days
services.referral: Ask offender manager, resettlement worker or prison housing adviser to submit a consented referral to the chosen housing authority.
services.notes: Does not replace the person’s own homelessness application; retain confirmation and consent record.

services.name: Migrant Help asylum helpline
services.type: Asylum support, accommodation and financial-support advice
services.referral: Call for asylum-support and accommodation issues; use webchat / portal when phone privacy is difficult.
services.notes: For people seeking asylum; do not assume eligibility for mainstream benefits or housing.

services.name: Rainbow Migration
services.referral: Contact for LGBTQI+ asylum / immigration advice and support; request safe and confidential contact.
services.notes: Pair with Migrant Help and regulated immigration advice where relevant.

services.name: Modern Slavery and Exploitation Helpline
services.type: Modern slavery reporting and support signposting
services.referral: Call for confidential advice; 999 where someone is in immediate danger.
services.notes: Do not put a suspected exploiter’s details in a device they can access.

services.name: Op FORTITUDE
services.referral: Self-refer or refer with permission; tell them housing risk and service history.
services.notes: May provide individual accommodation support for veterans at most risk.

services.name: Veterans Aid
services.type: Emergency practical support for veterans in crisis
services.referral: Call for an initial crisis assessment; local councils must also assess homelessness applications.
services.notes: Open regardless of rank, ethnicity, gender, age or length of service.

services.name: Scope helpline
services.type: Disability benefits, rights and practical support
services.referral: Ask about benefit rights and disability evidence; route housing adaptations to the council too.
services.notes: Can help prepare for requesting reasonable adjustments from councils and services.

services.name: Disability Rights UK
services.referral: Use the website / helpline for rights information and form-support pathways.
services.notes: Not an emergency housing route; link to evidence checklist and council application.

services.name: Find an immigration adviser
services.referral: Use only regulated advisers / solicitors; record adviser registration and appointment details.
services.notes: Use alongside Migrant Help / Rainbow Migration, not as a replacement for emergency safety.

services.name: National Careers Service
services.referral: Use for employment and training after urgent safety, housing and income are stabilised.
services.notes: Do not make job-search completion a precondition of support.

services.name: National Databank / digital inclusion
services.type: Free data, devices and digital-access signposting
services.referral: Find a local Online Centre / data bank; app should show other offline routes where device access is unsafe.
services.notes: Useful for completing Homechoice and benefit forms, but privacy risks must be assessed.

services.name: Imaan
services.referral: Use online contact route; pair with housing and abuse services when needed.
services.notes: Community support, not a housing provider.

services.name: KeshetUK
services.type: LGBTQ+ Jewish community support and inclusion
services.referral: Use online contact route; pair with statutory housing help for homelessness.
services.notes: Community support, not a housing provider.

services.name: Friends, Families and Travellers
services.type: Gypsy, Roma and Traveller advice and advocacy
services.referral: Contact for advice on discrimination, accommodation and rights; link to local authority homelessness service too.
services.notes: Protect against discriminatory assumptions; record preferred identity terms.

services.name: Switchboard LGBT+ Helpline
services.referral: Call, webchat or email; use for immediate affirming conversation alongside practical routes.
services.notes: Not specialist housing advice; use Stonewall Housing / akt in parallel.

services.name: HMRC digital / benefit identity support
services.type: Tax, National Insurance and proof-of-income support
services.referral: Use only where documentary evidence blocks work or benefit claims; provide alternatives where phone access is difficult.
services.notes: Supporting route, not a crisis route.

councils.route_notes: Online self-assessment or call. This number is stated as available 24/7.
Complete the quick online form; council housing register help line verified separately.
Contact Housing Solutions through the council form; response aims stated on page.
Complete the referral form and call if already homeless.
Use the homelessness web route in daytime; call out of hours only when homeless with nowhere tonight / health-safety emergency.
Contact Housing Options early; use council page for contact / assessment.
Call 01622 602127 for nowhere safe tonight; 01622 602000 for urgent housing help.
Call or email housing@sevenoaks.gov.uk; council runs advice drop-ins.
Contact Housing Options through Kent Homechoice / council enquiry route within 56 days or when homeless.
Use Housing Options / Kent Housing Group; 01843 577277 also used for rough-sleeper reports.
Contact housing services; same number appears for out-of-hours homeless emergency advice.
Call or visit The Amelia Scott; housingadvice@tunbridgewells.gov.uk is listed in the factsheet.
Adult route via Housing Options; not part of Kent County Council.

triage_routes.trigger_name: Immediate danger or severe medical emergency
triage_routes.recommended_action: Show 999 first; offer 111 / Release the Pressure after immediate safety action.
triage_routes.safety_note: Never wait for an online form.

triage_routes.trigger_name: No safe place to sleep tonight
triage_routes.recommended_action: Show the person’s council emergency route plus Porchlight / StreetLink. For danger from abuse, show KMDAP and Galop first.
triage_routes.safety_note: Ask only minimal questions: location, safety, age, household, safe way to contact.

triage_routes.recommended_action: Start local council homelessness application; then Shelter, Citizens Advice, debt support and evidence checklist.
triage_routes.safety_note: Do not say the person must leave at the end of a notice without legal advice.

triage_routes.recommended_action: Show council / Children's Services depending on age plus akt, Centrepoint, Stonewall Housing and BeYou.
triage_routes.safety_note: For under 18, Children's Services must be shown before adult routes.

triage_routes.trigger_name: LGBTQ+ person fleeing abuse or hate crime
triage_routes.recommended_action: Show 999 if immediate danger, then Galop, KMDAP / Medway DA service and council homelessness route.
triage_routes.safety_note: Include quick exit, browsing/privacy warning, and safe-contact field.

triage_routes.recommended_action: Show 999 if danger. Kent: Children's Social Care. Medway: youth homelessness / Children's Services. Also Centrepoint and akt where relevant.
triage_routes.safety_note: Do not require a parent’s permission to seek safety help.

triage_routes.trigger_name: Mental health or medication affected by homelessness
triage_routes.recommended_action: Show 999 where life at risk; 111 / Release the Pressure; GP without fixed address; request evidence for housing needs.
triage_routes.safety_note: Do not make housing advice conditional on mental-health treatment.

triage_routes.recommended_action: Show 999/111 for urgent symptoms; local treatment route; council housing route in parallel.
triage_routes.safety_note: Never say treatment is a prerequisite for housing help.

triage_routes.recommended_action: Ask release date; request consented Duty to Refer; show council and Nacro. If veteran, add Op FORTITUDE.
triage_routes.safety_note: Start no later than 56 days before release where possible.

triage_routes.recommended_action: Do not assume mainstream eligibility. Show Migrant Help, regulated adviser directory and Rainbow Migration for LGBTQI+ needs.
triage_routes.safety_note: Use a confidential interpreter and do not store immigration documents without consent.

triage_routes.trigger_name: Financial shock, food or energy crisis
triage_routes.recommended_action: Show KCC crisis support, food finder, benefits / debt support and local council prevention route.
triage_routes.safety_note: Do not treat a food referral as a solution to homelessness.

triage_routes.trigger_name: Disability, long-term illness or access need
triage_routes.recommended_action: Show GP access, Scope / Disability Rights and council. Capture requested adjustment and evidence separately.
triage_routes.safety_note: Examples: text contact, BSL interpreter, wheelchair access, quiet appointment, advocacy.

scripts.title: Presenting to the council: homeless tonight
scripts.script_text: I am homeless tonight and I have nowhere safe to stay. I want to make a homelessness application today. My safe contact method is [method]. I am [alone / with children / pregnant / disabled / at risk of violence / other]. Please record that I need an assessment and tell me what temporary accommodation or emergency help is available tonight.
scripts.use_note: Replace bracketed details only; ask for the officer’s name, reference number and written confirmation.

scripts.title: Presenting to the council: risk within 56 days
scripts.script_text: I am threatened with homelessness within 56 days because [notice / asked to leave / rent arrears / unsafe home / other]. I want to make a homelessness application and receive a personalised housing plan. I can provide [notice, tenancy, messages, medical evidence]. Please tell me the next appointment and how to send evidence safely.
scripts.use_note: Do not state that you have left if you have not. Keep copies of notices and messages.

scripts.title: LGBTQ+ safety and privacy request
scripts.script_text: I am LGBTQ+ and I need this information handled confidentially. It may not be safe to contact me by [phone / email / post]. Please use [safe method] and do not contact [name / address] without asking me first. My safety concern is [brief description].
scripts.use_note: The app should make this an optional protected field, never displayed in notifications.

scripts.title: Requesting a Duty to Refer
scripts.audience: Prison, hospital, Jobcentre, social worker, probation or clinician
scripts.script_text: I am homeless or at risk of homelessness within 56 days. I consent to you making a Duty to Refer to [council]. Please give me a copy or reference, record my safe contact method, and tell me what follow-up I need to make myself.
scripts.use_note: Consent is required. The person should still approach the council directly where possible.

scripts.title: GP registration with no fixed address
scripts.script_text: I am currently of no fixed abode / staying temporarily locally. I want to register with this GP. I understand I can register without proof of address or ID. If you need a contact address, please use [care-of address / practice address if offered]. I also need an appointment about [health issue] and a letter describing how this affects my housing if clinically appropriate.
scripts.use_note: If refused, ask for the practice manager and use NHS England guidance in the app.

scripts.title: Requesting reasonable adjustments
scripts.script_text: Because of [disability / health / hearing / communication need], I need these reasonable adjustments: [text/email contact, interpreter, accessible venue, longer appointment, advocate, quiet waiting space]. Please confirm what you can provide and how I should send evidence.
scripts.use_note: Record the request, date, response and any agreed adjustment.

scripts.title: Landlord / agent: notice and repairs
scripts.script_text: Please confirm in writing the reason you are asking me to leave and provide all formal notices. I am seeking housing advice. I will keep paying rent where I can and I need communication in writing because [reason]. Please also respond to the repairs / safety issue reported on [date].
scripts.use_note: Do not advise a person to stop paying rent; refer to Shelter / Citizens Advice for case-specific advice.

scripts.title: Temporary accommodation suitability concern
scripts.script_text: I am concerned that the accommodation offered may be unsuitable because [violence risk / disability access / children / medical need / school or care needs / travel safety]. I can provide evidence. Please record this before placement and explain how I can request a review or raise safeguarding concerns.
scripts.use_note: Accepting accommodation can be complex; get case-specific legal advice before refusing.

scripts.title: LGBTQ+ specialist housing referral
scripts.script_text: I am [age] and live in / am currently in [Kent district]. My current housing is unsafe or unstable because [brief]. I am LGBTQ+ and need confidential, affirming housing advice. I can safely be contacted by [method/times]. My immediate risk tonight is [none / high / emergency].
scripts.use_note: Never include a person’s identity in a shared device notification.

scripts.title: Prison release housing plan
scripts.script_text: My release date is [date] and I do not have safe accommodation. Please start or update my resettlement housing plan, make a consented Duty to Refer to [council], and give me copies of my release, risk, benefit and ID documents. I need safe contact by [method].
scripts.use_note: Start at least 56 days before release when possible.

scripts.title: Asylum / immigration safe request
scripts.script_text: I am concerned about homelessness / accommodation and need confidential advice about my status. I am LGBTQI+ [optional] and have safety concerns. Please tell me what housing or support route applies, what evidence is needed, and how you will contact me safely.
scripts.use_note: Do not submit immigration information through an untrusted shared account.

scripts.title: Help request to a trusted person
scripts.script_text: I’m at risk of having nowhere safe to stay. I don’t need you to solve everything; I need help making a housing call / getting to an appointment / keeping documents / having a safe contact address. Would you be able to help with [one specific thing] today?
scripts.use_note: Keep the ask small and specific; never pressure someone to disclose identity or abuse details.

evidence_checklist.useful_evidence: Photo ID if available; National Insurance number; safe email/phone; trusted contact
evidence_checklist.safety_note: Useful but lack of ID must not block emergency help or GP registration.

evidence_checklist.useful_evidence: Tenancy, licence, rent book, landlord details, council-tax record, messages showing asked to leave
evidence_checklist.safety_note: Take screenshots that show dates and sender; store copies safely.

evidence_checklist.useful_evidence: Section 8/21, possession claim, hearing notice, bailiff warrant, lockout evidence
evidence_checklist.safety_note: Do not ignore court documents. Route urgently to Shelter / HLPAS / legal advice.

evidence_checklist.useful_evidence: UC journal, payslips, bank statements, rent arrears, utility / council-tax arrears
evidence_checklist.safety_note: Redact card numbers before sharing with anyone except verified official services.

evidence_checklist.useful_evidence: Prescription list, discharge papers, clinician letters, accessibility / care needs
evidence_checklist.safety_note: Ask clinician to describe functional impact and risk; not to make a legal housing decision.

evidence_checklist.useful_evidence: Child benefit, birth certificates, MATB1, school / care arrangements
evidence_checklist.safety_note: Show council promptly; never delay for documents where safety is urgent.

evidence_checklist.useful_evidence: Incident log, photographs, messages, crime reference, risk assessment
evidence_checklist.safety_note: Only store if safe. App should have protected storage, quick exit and delete/export controls.

evidence_checklist.useful_evidence: Safe-contact preference, incidents of discrimination, support letters if willingly provided
evidence_checklist.safety_note: No one should have to prove LGBTQ+ identity to get homelessness help.

evidence_checklist.useful_evidence: Home Office paperwork, ARC, adviser details, accommodation letters
evidence_checklist.safety_note: Store securely; route to regulated advice / Migrant Help.

evidence_checklist.useful_evidence: Release date, probation contact, service record, resettlement plan
evidence_checklist.safety_note: Ask for a consented Duty to Refer and retain the reference.

evidence_checklist.useful_evidence: Service number, discharge papers, veteran card if held
evidence_checklist.safety_note: Useful for Op FORTITUDE / Veterans Aid; absence should not stop general help.

evidence_checklist.useful_evidence: Date, service, worker, action, deadline, reference, outcome
evidence_checklist.safety_note: Create immutable timeline entries; user controls visibility and sharing.

sources.notes: Official Samaritans source. Free telephone support is available on 116 123, 24 hours a day. The UK email service stopped accepting new users on 27 April 2026 and is scheduled to close completely on 30 September 2026. Do not present jo@samaritans.org as a standard contact route for new users.
